title: Baseline: Continuous Maize Monoculture
verdict: VULNERABLE & UNSUSTAINABLE UNDER PROJECTED CLIMATE SHIFTS
nasa_evidence: NASA GPM decadal records demonstrate 32 dry spells (>= 5 days) during the growing season; conventional maize suffers severe yield drag when dry spells coincide with silking.
NASA POWER indicates 34 annual heat stress days (Tmax >= 35°C), coinciding with tassel flowering in unprotected monoculture.
NASA SMAP confirms topsoil (0-5cm) dries out in < 4 days, leaving bare post-harvest soil vulnerable to high rainfall erosivity (MFI > 140).
agronomic_vulnerabilities: Net soil nitrogen depletion of 75.0 kg N/ha per year, requiring heavy synthetic fertilizer expenditure (GHS 1800.0/ha).
Continuous host plant presence intensifies Fall Armyworm (Spodoptera frugiperda) pest pressure.
Monoculture price volatility exposes the farm family to single-crop market collapse.

title: Scenario 1: Regenerative Climate-Resilient Rotation
verdict: TOP RECOMMENDATION FOR CLIMATE RESILIENCE & FOOD SECURITY
core_strategy: Drought-Tolerant Maize + Relay Cassava (Major Season) -> Nitrogen-Fixing Cowpea (Minor Season)
why_it_wins: Increases net farm profit by +237.9% over baseline (GHS 23652.0 vs GHS 7000.0).
Cuts synthetic fertilizer expenditure by GHS 780.0/ha by leveraging cowpea biological nitrogen fixation (+15.0 kg N/ha net budget).
Extends living soil cover from 4.5 months to 10.0 months, suppressing weeds and shielding topsoil from torrential storm runoff.
Dramatically enhances household protein yield (+345.3 kg protein/ha) via high-protein cowpea pulses.

nasa_decision_triggers.planting_trigger: Wait for NASA GPM 3-day rainfall >= 20mm after March 20 AND SMAP root-zone moisture anomaly Z > 0.0 before sowing maize/cassava.
nasa_decision_triggers.dry_spell_mitigation: Cassava roots penetrate 0-100cm, tapping subsoil water reserves identified by SMAP during mid-season dry spells.
nasa_decision_triggers.minor_season_trigger: Sow short-duration Cowpea (65 days) by September 10 to mature before November Harmattan cessation.

trade_offs_and_management: Cassava harvesting requires distributed family or hired labor over an extended window.
Requires access to certified pest-resistant cassava cuttings (Bankyehemaa) and early cowpea seed.

title: Scenario 2: Commercial Agro-Economic Diversification
verdict: HIGH PROFIT OPTION FOR CAPITALIZED COMMERCIAL GROWERS
core_strategy: White Yam (Pona) + Border Maize (Major Season) -> Commercial Soybean (Minor Season)
why_it_wins: Generates maximum net economic return (GHS 35730.0 / $2382.0), nearly tripling baseline revenue.
Soybean commands robust guaranteed cash markets in Ghana for poultry feed and cooking oil processing.
Soybean nodulation fixes +45 kg N/ha, replenishing soil nutrients after heavy yam feeding.

nasa_decision_triggers.soil_workability_trigger: Plant yam mounds only when SMAP surface moisture reaches 0.40 - 0.60 fraction (prevents clodding).
nasa_decision_triggers.tuber_bulking_alert: Monitor SMAP root-zone moisture in July/August during yam tuber expansion.

trade_offs_and_management: High upfront capital requirement: Yam seed setts require substantial initial investment (GHS 3,200/ha).
Mounding, staking, and yam vine maintenance require intensive labor.
Higher vulnerability to severe mid-season droughts than cassava.
